verdicts.rationale: Mechanism verified end-to-end. extractHeadings stamps `id: heading-${idx}` where idx is the top-level doc.content array position (OutlinePanel.tsx:308 forEach + :322). The collapsed Set is keyed purely by these strings — toggleNode/collapseAll/expandAll mutate it with `h.id`/`pod.id` (OutlinePanel.tsx:1545,1593-1597), render-time membership tests use the FRESH per-pass id (:66,:600,:1126), and the Set is persisted verbatim (saveOutlinePrefs `collapsed: [...collapsed]`, :1189) and rehydrated into a Set (loadOutlinePrefs → setCollapsed(new Set(saved.collapsed)), :1488). I grepped the whole file for any reconciliation/remap/prune of the Set against live heading ids — there is NONE. So inserting/removing a top-level block above a collapsed heading re-derives a new `heading-<idx±1>` id on the very next render; the previously-collapsed heading is no longer in the Set (auto-expands) and a different heading now at the old index renders collapsed. Reachable IN-session (next render after a structural edit, since render reads fresh ids vs old-pass Set strings) AND cross-session (reload after structure changed). Held at MEDIUM not upgraded: this corrupts VIEW STATE only (which sections are folded) — no document content is lost or rewritten, and the user can re-collapse. Held at MEDIUM not downgraded: the trigger (editing above a folded section) is an extremely common action and the wrong-fold is silent. This is exactly the index-vs-UUID staleness the focus-view rework migrated away from (useFocusMode anchors on attrs.uuid); the outline collapse-set was left on the old pattern.
verdicts.correctedRootCause: Confirmed as finder stated. Deepest cause: persistent identity (the collapsed Set, both in-memory and the localStorage `virgil-outline-prefs.collapsed` array) is keyed on a live array index (`heading-${idx}`, OutlinePanel.tsx:322) that extractHeadings regenerates on every pass (:308), with no remap layer. saveOutlinePrefs:1189 / loadOutlinePrefs:1488 persist/restore the raw index strings.
verdicts.class: Persistent/cached structural identity keyed on a live array index instead of a stable UUID. In-file sibling: buildPods reuses `h.id` for edit-mode pod collapse (OutlinePanel.tsx:800,806) inheriting the same drift. Contrast self-healing index attrs (`data-outline-pos="h-${index}"`, posToAttr:97) which are recomputed live each render and so never corrupt. The whole focus subsystem (useFocusMode/focus-view) is the correct UUID-anchored counter-example.

verdicts.rationale: Two divergent doc snapshots feed the outline subsystem and the divergence window is real. (1) The panel RENDERS from a live snapshot: every docked/floating OutlinePanel gets content={editor.getJSON()} captured at React render time (EditorPane.tsx:3400,3473), so the clicked row's blockIndex reflects the live doc. (2) The focus action handlers read a STALE heading map: outlineHeadings = extractHeadings(latestDoc).headings (EditorLayout.tsx:2360-2361) and latestDoc is set inside a 300ms setTimeout in handleUpdate (editor-ops.ts:41-48). useFocusActions threads that stale list into focusMode.moveTo/expandTo/snapBoundary (focus.ts:25-38). I confirmed moveTo (useFocusMode.ts:292-300) reads the LIVE doc (editorRef.current.state.doc) then computes sectionRange(blockIndex, STALE headings, STALE totalBlocks) (:296) and bandFromIndices against the LIVE doc (:297 → :99-113) — fresh index meets stale section map → [start,end] resolves to the wrong live blocks. The window is genuine: useStructuralRevisions bumps synchronously off DocStructureBus (useStructuralRevisions.ts:90-128) → EditorPane re-renders with fresh getJSON() well before the 300ms latestDoc debounce settles. Held at MEDIUM: the misfire is transient (self-heals on the next interaction / once latestDoc settles), the band is UUID-anchored at write so it lands on a real-but-wrong section (recoverable, no persisted corruption, no content loss), and the trigger requires a heading-position-shifting structural edit followed by a focus interaction within 300ms — narrow, but plausible when an AI agent batches structural edits while the user is interacting.
verdicts.correctedRootCause: Confirmed as finder stated. Canonical fix would be to source outlineHeadings/outlineTotalBlocks from the SAME live snapshot the panel renders from (a rev-gated editor.getJSON()) rather than the 300ms-debounced latestDoc (EditorLayout.tsx:2360 docForOutline = latestDoc; editor-ops.ts:45 setLatestDoc behind setTimeout).
verdicts.class: Mixing a debounced doc snapshot (latestDoc) with live-doc index math where the index originates from a fresher snapshot. In-file siblings: focusWordCount sums per-block counts over the focus range using buildPerBlockCounts(docForOutline=latestDoc) (EditorPane.tsx:2387-2392) — transient count wobble; handleFocusActivate uses the same stale outlineHeadings[0].index (focus.ts:22). availableDividerLevels (EditorLayout.tsx:2363-2369) also derives from the stale outlineHeadings but is cosmetic.

verdicts.rationale: Confirmed: nothing gates the label commit on the conflict. InlineLabel computes `conflict` (OutlinePanel.tsx:185-186) purely to drive the warning class/message, and commit() unconditionally calls onCommit(trimmed || null) (:179-183) on both Enter (:196) and blur (:199). The downstream handleUpdateLabel does NO taken-key check either — it just setNodeMarkup({...attrs, label}) (editor-ops.ts:148-151). The central isLabelTaken registry (labels.ts:54-63, threaded via EditorLayout.checkLabelTaken :896-902 → OutlinePanel isLabelTaken prop :2830) is advisory only. I ALSO verified the finder's suspected sibling: the main-editor heading-label input has the identical pattern — refreshWarning only toggles a CSS class/warning div (editor-extensions.ts:986-996) while commit() writes label:newLabel via setNodeMarkup (:1051) with no conflict bail (:999-1081). So the defect-class is real and present in BOTH label-edit surfaces. Held at MEDIUM (not upgraded to DATA-LOSS): Virgil does not compile LaTeX and there is no in-app \ref→heading jump that mis-resolves on a duplicate (grep of labelRef paths shows label-matching only for rename propagation, editor-extensions.ts:1030,1066; labelRef carries a resolved displayText), so the immediate harm is two identical \label{} keys in preserved source — recoverable, surfaced by a live warning the user chose to ignore. The downstream consequence (LaTeX 'multiply-defined labels', \ref binds to last def) is real but deferred to compile time outside the app.
verdicts.correctedRootCause: Confirmed as finder stated. Warning-only validation: the conflict predicate is computed and rendered but never consulted at the write boundary (OutlinePanel.tsx:179-183 commit; editor-ops.ts:148 handleUpdateLabel; editor-extensions.ts:999-1081 main-editor commit).
verdicts.class: Warning-only validation that never gates the commit. CONFIRMED sibling: main-editor heading-label input (editor-extensions.ts:999-1081). Suspected (not verified here, out of subject scope): Bibliography rename-citekey collision path.

verdicts.rationale: The missing node-type guard is REAL: handleRenameParTitle (editor-ops.ts:160-174) calls setNodeMarkup(offset, undefined, {...node.attrs, parTitle}) at the matching index with NO node.type.name check, unlike handleRenameHeading (:129 guards 'heading') and handleUpdateLabel (:147 guards 'heading'). BUT the finder's primary claimed symptom — a ProseMirror RangeError — is technically WRONG, so the severity is materially overstated. I traced the write path in the installed libs: prosemirror-transform setNodeMarkup (dist/index.js:1133-1144) builds the new node via `type.create(attrs,...)` (:1139), which routes through NodeType.create→computeAttrs (prosemirror-model dist/index.js:2177-2180 → 2042-2056). computeAttrs iterates ONLY the node type's DECLARED attrs and silently ignores extra keys; the throwing checkAttrs (:2057-2060 'Unsupported attribute') is NOT on this path — it is only invoked by Node.check()/fromJSON (:1496,1540-1541), and the ReplaceAroundStep setNodeMarkup dispatches doesn't re-run it. Heading declares level/label/uuid/numbered/sectionNumber but NOT parTitle (editor-extensions.ts:772-779). So writing parTitle onto a heading produces a node recreated with its unchanged heading attrs and the parTitle value DROPPED — a benign, throw-free no-op (the rename simply does nothing). Add that the trigger (a parTitle pod's blockIndex diverging to a heading via a concurrent structural edit between render and click) is already the low-confidence, narrow case the finder admits. Net: real inconsistency, harmless effect → LOW, bordering COSMETIC.
verdicts.correctedRootCause: Real cause: handleRenameParTitle (editor-ops.ts:166-167) omits the `node.type.name === 'heading'`-style guard its sibling mutators carry. CORRECTED mechanism: on a heading the result is NOT a RangeError but a silent no-op — setNodeMarkup→type.create→computeAttrs (prosemirror-model dist:2042-2056) drops the undeclared `parTitle` key without validating; checkAttrs (which would throw) is not reached on the setNodeMarkup transform path (prosemirror-transform dist:1133-1144). parTitle is simply discarded; the heading is rewritten with identical attrs.
verdicts.class: Index-addressed structural mutators that omit the node-type assertion their sibling handlers carry (editor-ops.ts handleRenameParTitle vs handleRenameHeading/handleUpdateLabel). The graver members of this class are wrong-target WRITES on a snapshot-divergent index (the OUT-F8-02 class), not throws — e.g. renaming the wrong PARAGRAPH's parTitle if the index lands on a different paragraph rather than a heading.
